newsitem.title: GERMANY: G7 not sought higher dlr for some time - US official.
newsitem.headline: G7 not sought higher dlr for some time - US official.

text.p: The Group of Seven industrial nations have not sought a dollar appreciation for some time, a senior U.S. Treasury official said on Saturday.
"For some time now, the asymmetric position of April 1995 (pointing toward appreciation of the dollar) has not been the policy," the official, who declined to be named, said.

The G7, which includes Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, declared on Saturday that currencies were no longer significantly out of line and that excess volatility in exchange markets was not desirable.

The U.S. official said the G7 agreement recognizes that the recent decline in the currencies of a number of the group's members are a "matter of concern." Those members include Japan and some European countries.

The official stressed the importance of Japan following through with its commitment to promote strong domestic demand-led economic growth and said Tokyo may need to take further measures to ensure that.
"This is a commitment we, in the United States, take very seriously," he said, adding, "there is a real possibility that would require further action on Japan's part."
